name: Street Corn Chicken Rice Bowl

ingredients.buy: 2/3 cup crumbled; 1/2 cup crumbled, for topping
juice and zest of 3 1/2 limes; 7 tablespoons
1/2 cup chopped; 2/3 cup chopped; 1 1/2 cups leaves, for topping

writer_notes: Band confirmed from locked view: cal 597 (under 600, inside 450-800), protein 44.6 (>=40), rice supplies the required carb. Recipe qualifies.

All 20 locked ingredient lines are used by a step; no step uses an unbought item. Three cilantro measures map to rice/salad/topping, two sea-salt measures to spice blend/rice, two cotija measures to salad/topping. Plain 'Salt' line is the corn-salad quarter-tsp.
Scaling from source 4 servings to 14 is a uniform 3.5x and consistent across every line; no implausible quantity.

No cost_lines were supplied in this dispatch, so shop_smart carries NO per-package or per-ounce claim; cost/upsell use the ${{cost_ps}} token and no literal dollar figure. A later traced pass can add package math if the built spec exposes cost_lines.
Avocado and red onion (and the topping cotija/cilantro) are finishers, flagged in portion_html to be added at serve time, not packed into containers, to avoid browning and sogginess.
Jalapeno is optional in the source and kept optional in prose.
Macro references use {{protein}} and {{cal}} tokens; the 'under 600 calories' bound is written literal per rails.

prose.intro_html:
Mexican street corn, the elote you grab from a cart and eat over a napkin because it drips, is one of the great cheap pleasures in this world. The problem is you cannot exactly meal prep a stick of corn. So we did the sensible thing and turned it into a bowl. Spiced chicken, cilantro lime rice, and a creamy street corn salad that carries all the tang and cotija and lime you came for.

Here is why it earns a spot in your rotation. It lands at {{protein}} grams of protein a serving and stays under 600 calories, which is a rare combination for something that tastes like a treat. It cooks in one pot and one skillet, it reheats without turning sad, and every dollar in it is doing real work. This is comfort food that happens to be math you can be proud of.
prose.shop_smart:
The chicken is the engine here, so buy boneless skinless breast in the largest pack your store sells and cut it into one inch chunks yourself. Chunks cook faster and more evenly than whole breasts, and you never pay the premium for pre-cut.

Canned sweet whole kernel corn is the honest move for a fourteen serving batch. It is already cooked, it drains in seconds, and it holds up in the salad better than you would guess. Grab your cans in whatever multipack gets you to seven cups drained and you are set.

Cotija shows up in two places, the salad and the topping, so buy it once and crumble as you go. Same story with the cilantro and the limes. You are zesting and juicing across the rice, the salad, and the finish, so keep a few limes on the counter and do not toss a spent one until you have taken the zest first. Greek yogurt does the heavy lifting that sour cream usually gets credit for, and plain is the only kind you want. The jalapeno is optional, so buy it only if your crew likes a little heat.
prose.make_it:
Start the rice, because it runs on its own clock. Bring the water to a boil, stir in the rice and the sea salt, then cover it, drop the heat to low, and let it simmer about twenty minutes until tender. While it cooks, stir the chopped cilantro together with lime juice and lime zest in a bowl. When the rice is done, fold it into that cilantro lime mix warm so it drinks everything up.

Now build the street corn salad. In a bowl, combine the drained corn, Greek yogurt, cotija, mayonnaise, lime juice and zest, the diced jalapeno if you are using it, cilantro, and salt. Stir gently until it comes together, taste, and adjust. Set it aside so the flavors get to know each other.

Season the chicken. Combine the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and sea salt in a small bowl, then toss the chicken chunks in it until every piece is coated. Add the olive oil to a large skillet over medium heat, and once it is hot, lay in the chicken. Cook four to five minutes per side until it is cooked through and the internal temperature reaches 165 degrees. Do not crowd the pan, work in batches if you have to, because a crowded pan steams instead of searing.

To plate, spread the cilantro lime rice across the bottom, top it with the chicken chunks, and add a generous scoop of the street corn. Finish with avocado, red onion, a little more cilantro and cotija, and a squeeze of lime.
prose.portion_html:
This batch fills fourteen containers, and the honest way to split it even is to weigh, not eyeball. Weigh your empty container, then weigh the full pot of rice, the chicken, and the corn salad separately, divide each total by fourteen, and portion to that number. Your last container gets the same as your first instead of a sad scrape of what is left.

One thing about the toppings. The avocado and red onion, and the last sprinkle of cotija and cilantro, are finishers. Add them the day you eat the bowl, not when you pack it, because avocado browns and onion mellows in the fridge. Portion the rice, chicken, and corn salad into your fourteen containers now, and keep a small stash of toppings to scatter on at serving time. Every bowl reheats the same, and the fresh top tastes like you just made it.
prose.cost_closing_html:
Here is what makes this one sing on a budget. The showy stuff, the cotija and the lime and the avocado, is used in small amounts as accents, while the bulk of the bowl is chicken, rice, and canned corn, three of the cheapest ways to buy protein and carbs in the store. That is how you land a bowl that eats like street food at ${{cost_ps}} a serving.

Compare that to grabbing the same flavors from a fast casual line, where a single bowl runs you the better part of a twenty. Fourteen of these for what one of those costs is not a rounding error, it is a raise you gave yourself.
